clues.title: Landscape: steep green mountains from fjords
text: The landscape of the Faroe islands is characterised by long, wide fjords with jagged **green mountains** that rise straight out of the water, with rocky ridge lines along the mountainsides. The mountains generally look more imposing and greener than coastal mountains in Iceland, which can often be used to tell them apart.

images.caption: A still grey lake under rounded green hills with terraced slopes

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Long wide fjords with jagged green mountains rising straight out of the water and rocky ridge lines. Looks greener and more imposing than Iceland's coast.

differs.how: Iceland's coastal mountains are less green and less imposing

clues.title: Plants: almost no natural trees
text: The Faroe islands have **almost** **no naturally growing** trees.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Almost no trees grow naturally, so bare green hillsides are normal.

clues.title: Google car: blurred black pickup, front antenna
text: The generation 4 coverage was captured with a black pickup truck with an antenna on the front. The truck is always blurred.
NOTE: The truck in Iceland does not have a similar antenna.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Gen 4 coverage uses a black pickup truck, always blurred, with an antenna on the front. Iceland's truck has no similar antenna.

differs.how: Icelandic truck has no front antenna

clues.title: Google car: black car, plain grey roof rack
text: All Generation 3 car coverage on the Faroe Islands has a black Street View car with a **plain grey roof rack**.
NOTE: No other country with a similar landscape has a car similar to this.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: All Gen 3 car coverage is a black car with a plain grey roof rack. No other country with a similar landscape has a car like it.

clues.title: Houses: wood with stone base, grass roofs
text: Faroese houses are typically made of wood, often with an **above ground basement** made of stone which is painted in a different colour than the wooden part. Roofs will usually be either metal or have **grass on top** (turf).

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Wooden houses, often on a raised stone basement painted a different colour. Roofs are metal or covered in grass (turf).

clues.title: Language: Ð and Á letters, plus Ø
text: The Faroese language is most closely related to Icelandic, with the special letters Á, Ð, Í, Ó, Ú, Ý, Æ and Ø. It differs from Icelandic by using the letter **Ø**, while Icelandic uses É and Þ.

images.caption: Faroese text with the letters Ð Á Í Ó Ú Ý Æ Ø shown large

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Uses Á, Ð, Í, Ó, Ú, Ý, Æ and Ø. Seeing Ø separates it from Icelandic, which uses É and Þ instead.

differs.how: Iceland uses É and Þ, not Ø

clues.title: Bollard: small wooden stick, yellow top
text: Faroese bollards are small wooden sticks that are mainly painted **yellow **and sometimes** red on the top. **

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Small wooden sticks, mostly painted yellow and sometimes red on top.

clues.title: Guardrail: yellow reflectors
text: Guardrails on the Faroes have yellow reflectors.
NOTE: Yellow reflectors are not found on guardrails in any other northern European countries.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Guardrails carry yellow reflectors. No other northern European country does this.

clues.title: Sign: yellow direction sign, thin black border
text: Directional signs are **yellow** with a **thin black border** and a metal frame, very similar to the ones in [Iceland](https://maps.app.goo.gl/5HsMnQt8A7fSwKpo6).

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Yellow direction signs with a thin black border and a metal frame. Almost the same as Iceland's.

clues.title: Towns: only place with tall buildings
text: Torshavn is by far the **biggest town** on the islands, and the only place where you will find buildings taller than three floors. The landscape is somewhat open relative to the rest of the country, particularly to the east.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: The biggest town is the only place with buildings over three floors. The surrounding landscape is fairly open, especially to the east.

clues.title: Landscape: narrow fjord with steep hills
text: Klaksvik is the second biggest town in the country by a significant margin and can often be recognized by the **narrow fjord** with fairly steep hills going roughly north to south.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: The second biggest town sits by a narrow fjord with steep hills running roughly north to south.

clues.title: Landmarks: wind parks
text: There are three **wind parks** visible on the Faroes. The largest one by far is northwest of Torshavn, while the other two are [northeast of Torshavn](https://goo.gl/maps/JzeesXJKHpeXHzXU9) and [east of Vestmanna](https://goo.gl/maps/mMy1JQsEthsYG5z18) respectively.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: Three wind parks exist: the largest northwest of the capital, one northeast of it, and one east of Vestmanna.

clues.title: Houses: black houses with grass roofs
text: The village of Kirkjubøur at the southern tip of the main island can be recognised by the **black houses**, almost all having **grass roofs**. The town also has a small [church ruin](https://goo.gl/maps/iKdyAK21o3jhrJFh7).

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: A village at the southern tip of the main island has black houses, almost all with grass roofs, plus a small church ruin.

clues.title: Coverage: low narrow peninsula, island trekker
text: The trekker on Koltur island can typically be recognized by the narrow and low **peninsula** on the southeastern tip of the island.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: On the small island of Koltur, the trekker usually shows a narrow, low peninsula at the island's southeastern tip.

clues.title: Coverage: very low clouds around a peninsula
text: The trekker on Eiðiskollur can be recognized by the extremely **low clouds** surrounding the peninsula.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: The trekker on Eiðiskollur shows extremely low clouds surrounding the peninsula.

clues.title: Coverage: wide strait with islands behind
text: The trekker west of Skopun can be recognised by the **wide strait** to the north with the main islands of the Faroes in the background.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: The trekker west of Skopun looks north over a wide strait with the main islands in the background.

clues.title: Landscape: two pyramid mountains, thin snow
text: There are two distinct **pyramid-shaped mountains** to the south of the trekker on Klakkur, with a very thin layer of snow on top.

images.caption: Circle shows a small route map over a view of twin peaks above a fjord

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: The trekker on Klakkur sees two distinct pyramid-shaped mountains to the south, with a very thin layer of snow.

clues.title: Coverage: village below snowy mountains
text: The trekker by Gjógv features a view of the **village to the south** with snow covered mountains in the background.

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: The trekker by Gjógv looks south over the village, with snow-covered mountains behind.

clues.title: Boat: grey boat with reflective clothing
text: A **grey boat** featuring several people in **reflective clothes** and with the text “RIB62” can be seen going to Koltur island.

images.caption: Several people in reflective clothing on a grey boat, speeding across the water

credit.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

clues.summary: A grey boat with several people in reflective clothes and the text 'RIB62' heads to Koltur island.
